summary: Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says all types of visa can be applied for through its online visa portal, describes visas acquired at Iran's international airports, and lists the countries whose citizens are subject to visa waiver rules. It says some types of visa for the citizens of some countries are applied for only in person at an Iranian embassy, and that the citizens of some countries may not be issued a visa due to political and diplomatic considerations, without naming them. The UK Foreign Office says the Iranian Embassy has told it that British passport holders must apply as part of an organised tour or have a sponsor in Iran.

passportValidity.text: Iran's Foreign Ministry eVisa portal says that to apply for any electronic visa your passport should have at least six months of validity beyond your actual travel date, and its visa-on-arrival page says all visitors must hold a passport or travel document valid for 6 months at the time of departure. The UK Foreign Office says that if your passport has stamps from Israel or other countries' border crossing points with Israel, you may be refused entry to Iran.

notes: The UK government says it is illegal to import, sell, manufacture or drink alcohol in Iran, and that importing pork products is illegal.
The UK government says you need permission from the Iranian authorities to import or use equipment like drones or satellite phones; using them without permission is illegal and you could be arrested.

Canada's travel advice says Canadians have been denied entry into Iran because their passports bore an Israeli visa, an Israeli border stamp or an Egyptian or Jordanian border stamp issued by an office bordering Israel.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Iran's economy is exclusively cash-based: credit cards aren't accepted and ATMs exist only for local banking. The UK government adds that non-Iranian debit and cash cards will not work, that it is illegal to change money on the street, and that euros and US dollars are more commonly accepted than British pounds.

safety.text: The UK, Canadian and Australian governments all advise against all travel to Iran: Canada cites the volatile security situation in the region, and Australia the volatile security situation, armed conflict, civil unrest and the risk of arbitrary detention. The UK says British and British-Iranian dual nationals face a very high risk of arrest, detention and questioning, and reports attacks and robberies targeted at foreign nationals and tourists, including by thieves posing as policemen.

tips.text: The UK government says Islamic codes of behaviour and dress are strictly enforced: in public, women must cover their heads with a headscarf and wear trousers or a floor-length skirt with a long-sleeved tunic or coat reaching mid-thigh or knee, and men should wear long trousers and long-sleeved shirts.

Iran's MFA visa portal says some types of visa for the citizens of some countries can be applied for only in person at an Iranian embassy, without naming the countries. Iran's Interests Section in Washington says applicants with United States, United Kingdom and Canada passports must apply only through travel agencies or their host in Iran, and the UK Foreign Office says the Iranian Embassy has told it that British passport holders must apply as part of an organised tour or have a sponsor in Iran. Canada's travel advice says a tourist visa is required, and the US State Department's advisory is Level 4: Do Not Travel.

Iran's MFA asks visitors intending to acquire their visa at Iranian international airports to apply online at least two days before travel and to submit a hardcopy of the Grant Notice to the Visa-On-Arrival counter at the airport; it says the visa fee is paid through banking terminals at the airport in euros.

Australia's Smartraveller says Iran does not recognise dual nationality, that foreigners in Iran, including dual nationals, are at a high risk of arbitrary detention or arrest, and that it can't guarantee access to consular services or legal representation.

The UK government says non-Iranian debit and cash cards will not work in Iran, that it is illegal to change money on the street, and that euros and US dollars are more commonly accepted at exchange offices than British pounds.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Iran?
faq.answer: Unless your country is on Iran's visa-waiver lists, yes. Iran's MFA says all types of visa can be applied for through its online portal and describes visas acquired at Iran's international airports, but also says some types of visa for the citizens of some countries are applied for only in person at an embassy, and that the citizens of some countries may not be issued a visa, without naming them. Its portal says citizens of Azerbaijan, Turkey, Syria, Georgia, Armenia, Egypt, China, Iraq, Oman and Kazakhstan are subject to visa waiver rules, and that ordinary passport holders from 27 further countries can stay 15 days for tourism once every six months. The UK, Canadian, Australian, German and US governments say their citizens need a visa (the US State Department excepts Kish Island); the UK Foreign Office says British passport holders must apply as part of an organised tour or have a sponsor in Iran.

faq.question: Can Americans visit Iran?
faq.answer: The US State Department says US passports are valid for travel to Iran, but its advisory is Level 4: Do Not Travel, and it lists a tourist visa as required except for Kish Island. Iran's Interests Section in Washington says applicants with United States, United Kingdom and Canada passports must apply only through travel agencies or their host in Iran. For British passport holders, the UK Foreign Office says the Iranian Embassy requires an organised tour or a sponsor in Iran.

faq.question: Can I visit Iran if I have been to Israel?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says that if your passport has stamps from Israel or other countries' border crossing points with Israel, you may be refused entry to Iran, and Australia's Smartraveller says Iranian authorities will refuse entry if your passport contains Israeli stamps or visas. Canada's travel advice says Canadians have been denied entry because their passports bore an Israeli visa, an Israeli border stamp or an Egyptian or Jordanian border stamp issued by an office bordering Israel. No official page we could read states Iran's rule for Israeli passport holders; Iran's MFA visa portal says only that the citizens of some countries may not be issued a visa due to political and diplomatic considerations.

faq.question: Can I use my credit card in Iran?
faq.answer: No. Canada's travel advice says the economy is exclusively cash-based, credit cards aren't accepted and ATMs exist only for local banking, and it advises bringing sufficient cash, preferably in U.S. dollars or euros; the UK government adds that non-Iranian debit and cash cards will not work.

faq.question: What is the dress code for women in Iran?
faq.answer: The UK government says Islamic codes of behaviour and dress are strictly enforced. In public places women must cover their heads with a headscarf and wear trousers or a floor-length skirt with a long-sleeved tunic or coat reaching mid-thigh or knee, and they may be asked to put on a chador before entering religious sites. It says the authorities have arrested and detained women and girls for not properly following dress codes, and that enforcement crackdowns can lead to large-scale arrests at any time.

faq.question: Is Iran safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK, Canadian and Australian governments advise against all travel to Iran, and the US State Department's advisory is Level 4: Do Not Travel. Australia's Smartraveller says foreigners in Iran, including dual nationals, are at a high risk of arbitrary detention or arrest; the UK government says British nationals and British-Iranian dual nationals face a very high risk of arrest, detention and questioning.
